title: Partners
purpose: Every hour reaches the client through the same rules, no matter who runs the floor. So a partner's site is as safe to sell as our own.
how: Two channels, same rules. Direct operations is our own team: about 135 phones in factories and warehouses. Delivery partners run about 135 of our phones with their own people, in hotels in four cities, in Mansoura, and on their own sites. About 270 phones in all, and the client sees one company.

No channel may skip a rule. Every wearer goes through onboarding screening. Every person has one account in their own name, created by KMSC. We review every video before the client sees it. We pay for accepted hours, minus fraud flags. These rules are what make the hours worth buying.

The founders agree every partnership. Adham closes it and owns the client relationship. Mano does the paperwork and Ahmed Alaa handles the money. Moharam works with the partner day to day. Partners are not on the org chart, on purpose. Their people are not KMSC staff and never contact the client.

breaks.what: A partner's wearer filmed but never passed onboarding screening
breaks.do: Take the phone off the wearer right away. Moharam confirms within the hour. Youssef Medhat holds every session from that phone and sends none. Tell Mano the same day. Those hours are not paid. Moharam screens every wearer on that site again before filming restarts.

breaks.what: A partner site is holding more than one day of footage
breaks.do: This is an incident, same as on our own sites. Tell Moharam the same day. The partner uploads everything tonight on their own internet, as the agreement requires. If that fails, our runner takes all the site's phones to the nearest hub in one trip, under the transport rules, or the Planning and Logistics Lead fixes the line. No phone stays full overnight anywhere.
Hold the payment until the count is done. The agreement allows this. Moharam tells Adham the same day.

breaks.what: A partner stops answering, or leaves with our phones
breaks.do: Find the phones with MDM and put them in lost mode within the hour. You have 24 hours to get them back. After that, wipe the phones, file a police report, and update the phone list. Hold all payments. Tell Adham the same night. The 7-day exit period starts.

No hour on the shared account is paid, and the account is closed. The partner puts every wearer on that site through onboarding screening again before filming restarts. If it happens again, Adham decides whether the partnership continues.

questions.q: Why use our phones on a partner's floor, not theirs?
questions.a: The phone is how we keep control: MDM, kiosk mode, the map, and the wipe. On their phones we only have their word. On ours we have the count.

questions.q: A partner's people are already trained. Do they still go through onboarding screening?
questions.a: Yes. Every wearer in every channel does: ID copy, consent form, fraud briefing, one account, and the wearer log. Trained is not the same as having the right paperwork.

questions.q: What does a partner get paid?
questions.a: The rate is in their agreement only, never on this site or in a chat. How we pay is no secret: accepted hours, minus fraud flags, after the audit.

questions.q: Can a partner talk to the client?
questions.a: Never. Not the owner, not the site lead, not a wearer. Anything about the client goes to Moharam first, then Adham.

questions.q: Who fills in the daily report on a partner site?
questions.a: The partner's site lead. They submit the daily report form by 6:00 PM every day, one per site. We train them on the form on launch day. A day with no report is not paid.

partners.name: Direct operations
partners.model: KMSC staff on KMSC phones. We run everything ourselves.

partners.name: Delivery partners
partners.where: Hotels in four cities, Mansoura, and their own sites
partners.model: Their sites and people, our phones and standards. Their site lead submits the daily report form every day. The Planning and Logistics Lead sets the phone count per site.

agreement.term: Pay for accepted hours, minus fraud flags
agreement.text: The partner is paid on our own audit: accepted hours, after the month-end audit, with flagged footage taken off first. Sites, workers, and staff are paid the same way. Nobody is paid for a flagged hour, and a partner is not paid for a day with no daily report.

agreement.term: The partner must follow our rules to be paid
agreement.text: Every wearer goes through onboarding screening: ID copy, age 18 or older, signed consent form, signed fraud briefing, one account in their own name, and an entry in the wearer log. We review every video. Hours on an account with no paperwork, or a shared account, count as zero.

agreement.term: Our phones stay under MDM, with custody and return rules
agreement.text: The phones belong to the company, even on the partner's premises. They stay enrolled and supervised, with the collection app in kiosk mode, and on the map at all times. Both sides sign at handover and at every transfer. Phones stay at the site, at a hub, or in the provided bag someone signed for. They never go to anyone's home.

agreement.term: The partner must upload footage and submit the daily report every day
agreement.text: The partner uploads the footage from every phone every day, on their own internet, tested on launch day, or through a hub under our transport rules. No phone keeps more than one day of footage overnight. A site holding more than one day of footage is an incident. The partner's site lead submits the daily report form for every site by 6:00 PM. No report, no pay for that day.

agreement.term: The partner must follow our data-protection rules
agreement.text: Same data-protection rules as ours: consent before filming, signs at the entrances, no filming in restrooms, locker rooms, prayer rooms, clinics, or offices, and no uploads through anyone's home. If a phone is lost, a clip leaks, or someone complains, the partner tells Moharam and Mano within the hour, so Adham can tell the client within our 24-hour limit.

We can visit the partner's premises, count the phones, read the wearer log, check the screening files, and walk the floor. We do this every quarter, and on any day Moharam asks. If the partner refuses, we hold the payment until the count is done.

agreement.term: Either side can exit within 7 days, with a phone count
agreement.text: Either side can end the partnership in writing, for any reason. Within 7 days every phone, mount, and charger comes back and is counted against the phone list. All accounts are closed for good, and we pay when the count matches.
